SCOPE 1.1 The method is suitable for the determination of tract amounts of lead Lead contents ranging from parts per in a variety of petroleum products. billion (ppb, 1 in 10s) to parts per million (ppm, 1 in 106) can bc determined. 2. OUTLINE OF THE METHOD 665*6/-7 : 543.064 : 546.815

IN

Institute of Petroleum Method So. IP 224168 T.

2.1 A known volume of sample is shaken with aqueous iodine monochloride solution when any lead compound present passes into the aqueous phase. Organolead compounds ai-e then converted to the inorganic form by boiling After the solution, and the excess reagent destroyed with sodium sulphite. addition of buffer solution, the lead is extracted as dithizonate and determined calorimetrically. 3. APPARATUS 3.1 Separating Funnels - glass stoppered and of sufficient capacity to accommodate the chosen sample size (for example, not more than 4 times the volume of sample plus reagents).
NOTE 1 All glassware shall be of horosilicate. Lubricate separating NOTE 2 - Stopcock grease is often a source of contamination. funnel taps with a polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) aerosol spray or employ I'TFE taps.

4.6 Sulphite-Cyanide Solution - Dissolve 250 g of hydrated sodium sulphite (Na,SOs.7H,O) in about 900 ml of distilled water. Delead the solution by extraction with successive portions of dithizone solution until the green colour of the dithizone extract is unchanged. Wash the solution with chloroform to remove the bulk of dissolved dithizone and allow to stand Separate off the chloroform phase and run until the aqueous phase is clear. the aqueous layer into a I-litre volumetric flask. Add 12.5 g of potassium cyanide *(CAUTION), and shake until dissolved. Make up the volume of the aqueous solution to 1 litre with distilled water. CA UNION : Handle potassium cyanide with rubber gloves in vented hood and rvash hands frequently. Drain excess and waste solutions in a hooded sink not used for the disposal of acids andflwh with water.

PREPARATION OF APPARATU6

5.1 All glassware used in the procedure shall be washed with nitric acid and then with distilled water immediately More use. New apparatus should be soaked in chromic acid for 24 hours prior to the above treatment. 6. CALXBRATION 6.1 Calibration curves shall be drawn prior to the spectrophotometric demrr&ation. 7.1.2 Into an appropriate size of separating funnel, add 10 f 0.2 ml of the iodine monochloride solution. (A reagent blank shall also be carried through these steps but omitting the sample.) Adjust the temperature of the sample at 13 to 18�C and accurately measure the appropriate volume of sample into the separating funnel. (For example volumes below 25 ml, add 25 ml of petroleum ether, kerosine or suitable low olefin hydrocarbon. The requisite quantity of diluent should be included in the blank determination to account for any trace of lead introduced with the diluent.) Stopper the funnel and shake for 3 minutes to thoroughly mix the contents. Allow to stand until the two layers have separated. (With high `olefin content basestocks it may be necessary to filter the mixture through a plug of lead-free glass wool into another separating funnel in order to observe the separation. The glass wool removes iodine addition products which collect at the interface.) Run the lower aqueous extract into a 1251ml conical beaker. (If the lower aqueous solution is pale yellow or colourless

IS : 1448 [P : 80]- 1973 repeat the extraction with 10 ml portions of iodine monochloride reagent until the colour of the reagent remains relatively unchanged.) Wash the petroleum layer with three lo-ml washes of distilled water adding all the washings to the beaker. 7.1.3 Place the beaker and contents on a hot-plate and boil for 1 minute to complete the decomposition of lead alkyls. Remove the beaker from the hot-plate and cool to room temperature. 7.1.4 Add saturated sodium sulphite solution dropwise until the precipiMake just alkaline tated iodine redissolves and the solution is decolorized. to litmus paper with ammonia. Transfer the solution quantitatively to a 250-ml separating funnel and allow to cool. Add 50 ml of buffer solution, shake well, .and by means of a pipette, add 10 ml of the dithizone solution. Shake for 30 seconds, and allow to stand until the two layers have separated. If sufficient dithizone has been added Note the colour of the aqueous layer. If it is colourless or palethis will have the well-defined orange colour. yellow, add the dithizone solution in lo-ml portions until the colour of the aqueous layer is a definite orange after further shaking for 30 seconds. Note the volume of dithizone solution added and use the same volume for the blank. 7.1.5 When the lower organic layer has cleared, run it into the appropriate optical cell and proceed as follows according to the type of equipment use d: a) Sfiectrojhotometer - Measure the absorption of the solution at 520 nm. Read off the micrograms of lead in the sample from the appropriate calibration curve. b) Comparator - Compare the sample solution with the calibrated disk, using the dithizone solution from the blank in the comparison cell. 8.
